sources.said: Ten weeks, or one day of editing for each two days of scheduled photography, whichever is longer. (7-505(b))

figures.finding: For US studio features 2006 to 2016, pre-production averaged 146 days and the principal photography period 106 calendar days, so prep ran about 1.4 times the shoot period in most genres.
figures.applies: US major-studio live-action features 2006 to 2016, dates from trade announcements (calendar days, not shooting days).
figures.replaces: Stands for the prep length relative to the shoot in the game's studio-film schedule.

sources.said: Across all the movies studied, the average movie spent 146 days in pre-production.
Horror had the smallest (average of 92 days prep for an 81-day shoot = 113% of the shoot time spent in prep) while most genres were around 140% of shoot time spent in pre-production.

figures.finding: Of 1,546 independent domestic UK films shot from 2003 to 2011, 25.1% were released in UK and Irish cinemas within two years of the start of photography: 11.6% under £0.5m, 37.9% at £0.5m to 2m, 59.2% at £2m to 5m, 71.4% at £5m to 10m and 83.3% above £10m; 67% of those not released reached festivals or other platforms.
figures.applies: UK independent domestic features (no US studio backing), production years 2003 to 2011, release tracked by Rentrak; BFI Statistical Yearbook 2014.
figures.replaces: Stands for the game's chance that a finished independent film gets a cinema release, rising with budget.

sources.said: Of the 1,546 independent domestic UK films shot between 2003 and 2011, 388 (25%) were released theatrically in the UK and Republic of Ireland within two years of principal photography (Table 8.1).
Of the films which do not achieve a theatrical release, 67% get shown via another medium or become available on other platforms

figures.finding: Of 422 independent UK films released within two years, 6.6% earned international box office of at least twice their budget, the BFI's proxy for profit: 3.3% under £0.5m, 4.9% at £0.5m to 2m, 8.7% at £2m to 5m and 14.8% at £5m or more.

value.proxy: box office in 19 territories at least 2x budget

figures.applies: UK independent domestic features, production years 2003 to 2011, released in at least one of 19 territories within two years; the ratio-of-2 proxy is untested below £500,000.
figures.replaces: Stands for the game's chance that a released independent film recoups (about 1 in 15, 1 in 7 above £5m).

sources.said: Overall, just under 7% of released films achieved the international box office to budget ratio of 2 (8% for films with budgets of £500,000 or more).
Previous RSU analysis suggested that if a low to medium budget British film generates worldwide box office revenues greater than twice its budget, it is likely to be in profit

figures.finding: Of 877 US independent narrative features shot in 2017, 40% got no theatrical release, 35% a nominal release with no reported box office, 8% grossed $1 to $100k and 17% over $100k.
figures.applies: US-produced independent narrative features shot in 2017 (123 later major-studio releases excluded), dataset built by Stephen Follows and Bruce Nash.
figures.replaces: Stands for the US release outcome of a finished independent film: only about a quarter earn reported box office.

sources.said: This revealed that 40% of independent films made in 2017 did not get any kind of theatrical release.
A further 35% had a nominal release, with no reported box office; 8% grossed between $1 and $100k; and 17% grossed over $100k.

figures.finding: The 2026 Sundance Film Festival chose 90 feature films from 4,255 feature-length submissions, about 2.1%.
figures.applies: Sundance Film Festival 2026 (announced 10 December 2025).
figures.replaces: Stands for the game's chance that a finished independent feature is selected by a top festival (about 1 in 47 at Sundance).

sources.said: The 2026 Sundance Film Festival program was selected from 16,201 submissions from 164 countries or territories, including 4,255 feature-length films.
The lineup announced today includes 90 feature-length films representing 28 countries and territories.

figures.finding: To join the Producers Guild in the feature category a producer needs a qualifying credit on at least two features released in the last seven years (ten for animation), each with qualifying US distribution; alternatively the p.g.a. mark on two features, or an Oscar or PGA Awards producing nomination within two years. Shorts need five in five years, scripted TV eight episodes in five years.

alternatives: Oscar or PGA Awards producing nomination within 2 years

figures.applies: United States, Producers Guild of America membership qualifications read 2026-11-01.
figures.replaces: Stands for the credits threshold at which the game's producer can join the guild: two distributed features inside seven years.

sources.said: To be eligible for consideration in the Producers Guild under the FEATURE FILM category, you MUST have a qualifying credit on a MINIMUM of TWO (2) FEATURE FILMS released within the last SEVEN (7) YEARS*, each with QUALIFYING U.S. DISTRIBUTION.
THE PRODUCERS MARK (p.g.a) – Producers granted “the Mark” (p.g.a.) on TWO (2) or more FEATURE FILMS with qualifying distribution. (*)

figures.finding: Telefilm's Production Program requires the producer to have produced at least a short film that screened at a qualifying festival or one hour of television with a producer or co-producer credit, or equivalent experience.

value.minimumPriorCredit: one short at a qualifying festival, or one hour of TV, as producer or co-producer

figures.applies: Canada, Telefilm Production Program Guidelines applicable as of 31 October 2025.
figures.replaces: Stands for the entry credit the game requires before a producer can apply to a national feature fund: one festival short or an hour of TV.

sources.said: and received either a Producer or Co-Producer credit or have equivalent producing experience.

figures.finding: O*NET's survey of US producers and directors (36 incumbents, August 2022) found the job asks for: no related experience 13.7%, over 6 months to 1 year 8.5%, 1 to 2 years 23.8%, 2 to 4 years 16.0%, 4 to 6 years 20.2%, 6 to 8 years 1.1%, 8 to 10 years 14.3% and over 10 years 2.5%; Job Zone 4 ('several years of work-related experience').
figures.applies: United States, O*NET 30.3 database (May 2026 release), incumbent survey dated August 2022; producers and directors are one occupation in O*NET.
figures.replaces: Stands for the years of related work before someone holds a producing job: about half need more than two years, a sixth more than eight.
